text: User corrected single-source verification of current events - multiple sources should be checked before reporting on news/political figures
User uses 'sorry continue' to resume after interruptions, expecting the assistant to pick up exactly where it left off

IIFE / scope-wrappers in JSX are a recurring smell the agent introduces; before adding any inline wrapper in JSX, check surrounding siblings for the prevailing pattern (inline prop or plain const) and conform to it.

Silently zero-defaulting missing fields in structured data (e.g., bounding-box coordinates defaulting to 0) produces fabricated downstream values that look valid; missing or partial data must be explicitly flagged rather than filled with silent defaults.

A terse 'keep going' continuation message after a frustrating turn does not grant license to advance to the next planned scope or phase; it resumes the current task only and carries the affect of the prior turn.

The user strongly prefers auto-generated or derived indices over hand-maintained ones; where a file has both policy and census sections, a marker-based split (e.g., '<!-- AUTO-GENERATED BELOW -->') lets the hand-written portion stay stable while the generated portion refreshes cleanly.

When formalizing a repeated manual workflow loop into a skill, implement the logic as testable shell scripts first and have SKILL.md call those scripts — this keeps the skill prompt readable and makes the logic independently verifiable.

Spawning a dedicated adversarial sub-agent (validator or skeptical-reviewer role) before declaring complex multi-phase work done consistently surfaces real blockers that the implementing agent missed; treat the adversarial pass as a required step, not an optional sanity check.

Framing each fix batch as 'this will fix it' or 'this addresses the gap' when the prior ship also made that claim and failed is a sycophantic pattern that erodes trust; if structural gaps have recurred, say so explicitly and describe the structural change, not just the additive fix.

High-cost agent modes (full multi-agent runs, expensive fan-outs) should default to a cheaper tier and require explicit user confirmation before escalating — surprising the user with a costly run when a lite mode would have sufficed breaks trust on cost.

When a user's repeated manual workflow becomes the de facto development loop across multiple sessions, that loop is a strong signal to formalize it as a named skill rather than re-establishing it from scratch each session.

When proposing a new storage backend (e.g., Redis) for a feature when an existing store (e.g., Mongo) is already in use, proactively justify the new dependency rather than waiting for the user to push back — the default should be 'use what's already there unless there's a concrete reason not to'.
